validity.researcher_notes: Existence and specs corroborated independently and precisely. The Arabic almasryalyoum.com article (already the sheet's own Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Start/Diameter/Owner ref) explicitly reads: 'وتمتد المرحلة الأولى من دهشور إلى الكريمات بطول 90 كم وقطر 36 بوصة' ("the first stage extends from Dahshour to Al-Kuraymat, length 90 km, diameter 36 inches") — an exact, independent match to GEM's StartLocation=Dahshour/EndLocation=Al Kurimat, LengthKnown=90, Diameter=36. The same article gives the whole-system figures (Dahshour→Aswan, 930 km, 30-32in) matching the P0477 SYSTEM/NETWORK aggregate row's 930 km total — confirms P0477 is GEM's deliberate network-summary row for this same six-segment system (P6697/P6698/P6699/P6700/P6701/P6702), per the documented segment-vs-network convention, NOT a duplicate pipeline (segment lengths 90+30+150+147+121+390=928≈930 and diameters 36,32,32,32,32,30 sum-match P0477 exactly in order). The Australian Pipeliner (pipeliner.com.au, 22 Sep 2009, independent English trade press, verified) and Petroleum Africa (petroleumafrica.com, 3 Jan 2011, independent, verified) both independently describe this same first stage as running 'from Cairo to a power station located near Beni Suef' — consistent with Dahshour (Giza, on the Cairo side) to the El Kureimat power-plant complex (Beni Suef border) being 'Al Kurimat'/'Al-Kuraymat'. Both English pieces are consistent with each other and with the Arabic source on the overall system (930 km, Giza→Aswan, LE5.7bn, 8→12 bcm/yr capacity) but do not themselves give the phase-1 90km/36in figures — those come only from the Arabic primary. Independent search also surfaced GASCO's real 'Dahshour compressor station' (est. Oct 2011 per Egyptian State Information Service reporting found via search, GASCO facility in Giza feeding gas south to Upper Egypt industry/power stations) — confirms 'Dahshour' as a real, named gas-transmission hub, not a phantom location. CAVEAT (not escalated to a concern, no better-sourced alternative found): StartYear1=2009 is consistent with the Pipeliner article's Sept-2009 description of stages 1-4 as 'most recently completed', but the same article says NVGC 'took over a pipeline built by the government' for phase 1 — implying this specific 90km stretch may predate 2009 as new construction (it could be an existing government line handed to the project). No independently sourced earlier date could be established, so 2009 is left as-is with this caveat noted. Separately, GulfPub (Tier-2, SDE Dec-2025 scrape) lists a 'South Valley Gas Pipeline' Dahsour→El-Koraimet segment with matching 36in diameter but only 56 km length (a 38% delta vs GEM's 90 km, auto-flagged). Given the exact, specific 90km figure independently corroborated by the primary Arabic press source, GEM's 90 km is judged correct and GulfPub's 56 km is the likely-erroneous figure here (Tier-2 does not override a corroborated GEM value) — no change recommended to LengthKnown.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Owner [ref] cites the same almasryalyoum.com URL used for Status/Diameter/Start — but I read the full article text and it never names ANY operating company (checked for 'شركة' [company], 'إيجاس' [EGAS], 'GASCO', 'Nile Valley' — none appear). So the current Owner value ('Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co', i.e. EGAS) is unsupported by its own citation. Independent evidence points elsewhere: (1) The Australian Pipeliner (pipeliner.com.au, 22 Sep 2009, verified, independent editorial trade press) states 'Petrojet has been constructing the 930 km pipeline for the Nile Valley Gas Company' — i.e. NVGC is the project owner/client, Petrojet the contractor. (2) GulfPub PE World Map (independent Tier-2 scraped dataset) lists operator='Nile Valley Gas Company' for every one of its six South Valley Gas Pipeline segment records, including the Dahsour→El-Koraimet segment matching this row. Both are independent of each other and of GEM. Background check (WebSearch, Egypt Oil & Gas / egyptoil-gas.com, 9 Jun 2020, independent Egyptian trade press, content read directly): confirms 'Nile Valley Gas Company (NVGC), a subsidiary of Taqa Gas' as a real, currently operating entity delivering gas in Beni Suef governorate — exactly this pipeline's corridor — corroborating NVGC's identity and its Upper-Egypt remit, though that 2020 piece describes household-distribution activity rather than trunk-pipeline ownership specifically. It is plausible EGAS (the state holding company) sits above NVGC/GASCO in the ownership chain, or that GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company, which also operates the Dahshour compressor station per an independent search hit) shares infrastructure responsibility — but no independent source names EGAS Holding Co directly as Owner of this specific segment, whereas two independent sources explicitly name NVGC. Tier: medium (1 strong independent primary trade-press source + 1 independent Tier-2 dataset, both pre-dating and independent of GEM; the current GEM value has zero support in its own citation).

routes.start_name: Dahshour (GASCO/Egyptian Natural Gas Co. compressor station), Giza Governorate
routes.end_name: Al Kurimat / El Kureimat gas-fired power-plant complex, Beni Suef Governorate border
routes.corridor_desc: First stage of the South Valley/Upper Egypt Gas Pipeline trunk: runs south from the Dahshour gas hub (Giza Governorate, ~35 km south of Cairo, near Dahshur village/necropolis, where GASCO operates a compressor station receiving gas from the Cairo-area/Delta grid) down the Nile Valley corridor to the El Kureimat thermal power-plant complex on the Beni Suef Governorate border, where the pipeline hands off to the next GEM segment (P6698, Al Kurimat→Beni Suef). Straight-line distance between the two named points is roughly 55-60 km; GEM's sourced 90 km pipe length implies a non-straight corridor (following the river valley / desert-edge alignment typical of Egypt's north-south gas trunks) rather than a direct line — no waypoint-level routing could be independently sourced, so the bound here is the two verified endpoints only, not a traced centerline.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established by name from the Arabic almasryalyoum primary source (Dahshour / Al-Kuraymat) and pinned with independently sourced coordinates: Dahshur village/site centroid from Wikidata Q685414 (29.793°N, 31.246°E) and the El Kureimat power-plant facility from Wikidata Q56360137 (29.2793°N, 31.2486°E, a named gas-fired thermal plant matching 'Al Kurimat'). No coordinates were invented — both are sourced facility/place coordinates. Could not independently source the actual pipe centerline/waypoints between the two points (no route map, GIS, or corridor description found beyond 'follows the Nile Valley south from Dahshour'), so suggested_route_accuracy is capped at medium (named, coordinate-pinned endpoints; unconfirmed intermediate routing) rather than high.

summary: P6697 (Dahshour-Al Kurimat, South Valley Gas Pipeline phase 1) confirmed real, correctly classified, and its 90km/36in specs precisely corroborated by an independent Arabic primary source (P0477 is the legitimate SYSTEM/NETWORK aggregate of this + 5 sibling segments, not a duplicate) — but Owner1 (EGAS Holding Co) is an attribution concern: its own citation names no company, while two independent sources (Australian Pipeliner 2009 + GulfPub) point to Nile Valley Gas Company (TAQA Gas subsidiary) instead. Suggested route accuracy: medium (named, coordinate-pinned endpoints; no sourced centerline). No UNRESOLVED items.
